commands.description: DESTRUCTIVE: unpair THIS DEVICE from its subdomain — deletes the local tunnel identity. K2 Connect is told only when this device's tunnel is connected (it holds the name); otherwise it is local only. The account keeps the subdomain. Not a pause; that is 'k2 tunnel disable'.

commands.name: tunnel forget
commands.description: Forget this device's tunnel locally (tunnel.json, frpc.toml, certificate) and tell K2 Connect NOTHING. For stale config from a migrated or cloned machine whose subdomain another box holds.

commands.name: tunnel subdomains
commands.description: Daemon-cached nested-subdomain routing map (label -> internal target + attributed workspace). Read-only; distinct from 'k2 publish subdomain list' (control plane).

commands.name: publish
commands.description: Host a daemon-owned process for this workspace (run/start/stop/rm/ps/logs) and manage nested Connect subdomains (status, subdomain create/list/point/rm/claim/unclaim). Default run creates a nested URL; --no-tunnel is local only. status is Connect plan, not process inventory (use ps).

commands.name: publish run
commands.description: Start a daemon-owned process for this workspace. Default (Pro) also creates nested https://<name>.<host>.k2.dev. --skin is a static HTML host (an app); prefer Next in cwd for new apps. Not k2 app (guests/roles/tokens). --no-tunnel is process-only (no Pro, no public URL). Same name already running: error — stop first. <name> is always required.

commands.name: publish frame
commands.description: Owner only. Which other sites may put a --skin App in a frame. Default: the App itself and K2's own windows (frame-ancestors 'self' tauri://localhost http://tauri.localhost). --allow adds https origins (at most 8); --none refuses every frame; --reset goes back to the default. Restarts the App if running. Bad origin exits 2; an agent passport exits 3 (owner_only). --cmd Apps set their own header: k2 study publish-framing.

commands.name: publish start
commands.description: Start a saved published service (uses stored --cmd/--port/--cwd). Do not pass them again.

commands.name: publish stop
commands.description: Stop a published service (kill the process). Nested URL stays until start or rm.

commands.name: publish rm
commands.description: Stop and forget a published service. Also removes the nested URL unless --keep-hostname. Distinct from 'k2 publish subdomain rm' (hostname only; does not kill a process).

commands.name: publish ps
commands.description: List hosted processes for THIS workspace (running/stopped, port, URL if any). Not Connect plan — that is 'k2 publish status'.

commands.name: publish logs
commands.description: Dump that process's log file (last N lines on GET). --tail follows.

commands.name: publish subdomain claim
commands.description: Adopt an existing nested subdomain label for the CURRENT workspace (daemon-local attribution; 'unclaim' drops it). create/point/rm stamp attribution automatically.

commands.name: connect
commands.description: Pair a purchased k2.dev subdomain to this device: account login (Supabase email/password or --token JWT), pick subdomain, write tunnel config, start tunnel. Nested Pro subdomains stay under k2 publish.

commands.name: connect login
commands.description: Sign in to k2.dev, list purchased subdomains, bind tunnel token via POST /cli/tunnel/config, start tunnel. Password is never stored (only ~/.k2/connect-account.json access/refresh tokens, 0600).

commands.name: connect status
commands.description: Show account session + paired subdomain + live tunnel status when the daemon is up.

commands.name: connect logout
commands.description: Clear ~/.k2/connect-account.json. Does not unpair the tunnel (use k2 tunnel release --confirm).

commands.name: users
commands.description: Local daemon connect-user accounts (GET/POST /cli/users*). list is default; add creates with interactive password or --password-stdin, then optional --role set-role; audit prints the last N auth-audit records (GET /cli/users/audit?tail=N, owner only); unlock clears a box login lock without changing the password.

commands.name: users unlock
commands.description: Clear a box login lock without changing the password. Exit 0 when no lock is present. Does not create a user.

commands.name: users add
commands.description: Create a local connect-user. Password via hidden prompt (+ confirm) or --password-stdin — never on argv. --role calls set-role after add (default member server-side).

commands.name: users pair-phone
commands.description: Make a one-time pairing code (10 minutes) plus a QR for the K2 Companion phone app (POST /cli/auth/device/pair-code). The owner token pairs as --user, else as the login linked to the owner; a login pairs only as itself and types its password again. Never from a browser. Exit 3 when refused.

commands.name: users phones
commands.description: List paired phones (GET /cli/auth/devices): the owner token or an Owner login sees everyone's, any other login its own. Also shows the login a new code pairs as.

commands.name: users unpair-phone
commands.description: End one paired phone (POST /cli/auth/device/revoke). The owner token or an Owner login may end anyone's, any other login its own. The phone then gets device_session_ended and must pair again.

commands.name: users set-can-clone
commands.description: Settings → Admin Access → Can clone (POST /cli/users/set-can-clone, owner only). Defaults on; Owners can always clone.

commands.name: clone
commands.description: Copy an agent (workspace, chat history, Thread, chosen vault secrets) to another server, this computer or a second copy here. People clone (clone gate: owner, or a login with Can clone; the personal-computer switch for pulls); agents propose and a person approves. Never prints a secret value. Exit 0 ok, 2 bad usage, 3 refused/unreachable.

commands.name: clone propose
commands.usage: k2 clone propose --to <host|here> [--no-threads] [--threads-since N] [--copy A,B] [--blank C] [--skip D] [--dest DIR] --why "…"
commands.description: Agents: hold a clone of your own workspace for a person (POST /cli/clone-proposal/new). Posts one Thread line for your human; you get a k2 msg when they approve, deny or it expires (7 days). k2 clone proposals --mine, k2 clone withdraw <id>.

commands.name: app
commands.description: Guests, roles, grants, and tokens for apps on this box (caps + rooms). Not a host — use k2 publish. Not desktop updates (k2 update --app). Separate from Connect users. Leftover: k2 skin.

commands.name: app validate
commands.description: Parse every JS/TS file and inline script of a published App's folder (or a workspace folder) with oxc and run the leak lints. Never runs the code. file:line:col per finding, each with a suggestion. Exit 0 no errors, 1 errors.

commands.name: app user add
commands.usage: k2 app user add <username> [--email e] [--password-stdin] [--app <app> [--role R]]
commands.description: Add an app principal (not a Connect user / not a /v1 API key). Optional email and password from stdin for K2 app login. Without --app the person gets the box login (host; owner only). With --app the person is a guest of that one App: its grant (the role, or no rooms) and no box login. An agent with "manage Apps" adds App users of its own workspace's Apps only.

commands.name: app user invite
commands.usage: k2 app user invite <username> --app <app> [--email e] [--role R] [--from <address>] [--json]
commands.description: Mail a person a one-time link to set their own password for one App (no password ever goes in the mail). A new person needs --email and is made App-only (that App's grant, no box login). The owner, or an agent with "manage Apps" for its own workspace's Apps: an agent's invite leaves from its workspace's address under its email sending mode (off: exit 3; approval: held, the link's clock starts when it is sent). No mail path: an agent is refused, the owner gets the link once. Links expire (invites 72 h by default; k2 app login settings).

commands.name: app user reset
commands.description: Owner only. A one-time reset link. When it is used, the password is set, every session ends, and extra access that waited for a reset (an agent made or set up this person) starts. The link is always K2's own set-password page (the box front door's /cli/skin/password/set, never an App's) with K2's fixed text. --code shows the link to you (the code alone when the box has no front door). Mailing needs --from <an address no agent can read> (a workspace mailbox could be read by its agent); it goes to the stored email, or --to (stored as their email on use). The stored email is refused for anyone an agent or App key set up (any tie: it could have chosen the address) and for an email from before 0.46.4 you haven't set since: use --to or --code. The front door must be https and no App's domain. An owner reset link lives 24 h (K2's, never the App's setting).

commands.name: app login settings
commands.description: An App's invite and reset links: how long they live (15m to 30d; invites 72h and resets 24h by default), its own set-password page (else the box front door's /reset), and its own subject and body ({app} {name} {username} {sender} {expires}; K2 always adds the link and the safety line itself). The owner, or the App's own agent with "...manage them end to end". No flags: show them. Also: k2 app invite-settings.

commands.name: app profile settings
commands.usage: k2 app profile settings <app> [--names on|off] [--image on|off] [--json]
commands.description: May an App's people change their own full and display names and their picture (both on by default). The owner or an Admin; the App's own agent with "manage its Apps' users" may only turn them off, for its own workspace's Apps. No flags: show them. See k2 study app-profile.

commands.name: app user show
commands.description: Owner only. A person's profile in one App: full name (a self-set one shows the username beside it), display name, email, picture hash, role there, last sign-in, sessions and the App's profile settings.

commands.name: app user image
commands.description: Owner only. Remove a person's profile picture (every App shows the same one).

commands.name: app user sessions
commands.description: Owner only. A person's signed-in browsers and devices in one App (coarse client label, never an IP); --revoke ends one (an id from the list), --revoke-all every one in that App.

commands.name: app user email
commands.description: Set or clear an app guest email. Omit or empty --email clears. Needed to mint a password-reset token.

commands.name: app user agent
commands.usage: k2 app user agent <username> <workspace> | k2 app user agent <username> --clear
commands.description: Owner only. Mark an app guest login as the agent of one workspace (handle or id), or clear the mark. Brokered db calls from a marked login stamp actor kind agent (k2.actor_kind()), so person-only policies refuse it.

commands.name: app user full-name
commands.description: Set or clear an app guest full name. Omit or empty --name clears. Not a secret.

commands.name: app user password
commands.description: Set or clear an app K2-login password. Empty stdin clears (cannot K2-login; static k2skn_ still works).

commands.name: app user unlock
commands.description: Clear an app guest login lock without changing the password. Exit 0 when no lock is present. Does not create a principal.

commands.name: app user list
commands.description: List app principals as username  full name|—  role|—  rooms|—  email|— (no secrets).

commands.name: app user remove
commands.description: Remove an app principal and their login sessions. Platform tokens survive.

commands.name: app user rooms
commands.description: Set default rooms for an unassigned guest (the box login). Assigned guests 400 until unassigned. --apply-tokens copies onto live sessions only (never platform tokens). --app sets the rooms of that guest's role-less grant on one App, creating it if missing (the owner, or an agent for its own workspace's Apps).

commands.name: app user role
commands.description: Assign an app role to a guest. Not Connect owner/admin/member. Re-assign replaces. Live sessions rewrite immediately.

commands.name: app user unassign
commands.description: Clear the assigned app role. Restores Thread-only + current default rooms on live sessions.

commands.name: app role
commands.description: Named bundles of scopes + agents for app guests. Not Connect roles. Not a platform-token role.

commands.name: app role create
commands.description: Create an app role. --agent optional (0 = Thread dark). Name charset is the same as usernames; Connect owner/admin/member (and the retired viewer) are rejected. --app tags the role for one App: it can only be used on that App's grants.

commands.name: app role list
commands.description: List app roles (name + caps + rooms; no secrets).

commands.name: app role room
commands.description: Add/replace functions on one room. Omit --caps = Thread-only. --clear drops that room.

commands.name: app role paths
commands.usage: k2 app role paths <role> <room> [--read a/,b/] [--write c/] [--upload d/] [--upload-dir c/in] [--download e/,f.pdf | --no-download] | --clear
commands.description: Folder path scope on one room line of a role (room-scope R3). Replaces the line's folders; unlisted folders are refused with the missing-cap 403. Works on any room the role holds and for agent logins alike.

commands.name: app role update
commands.description: Update a role. --clear empties rooms. Always rewrites live sessions of assigned guests (never platform tokens).

commands.name: app role remove
commands.description: Remove an unassigned app role. Assigned roles 400 until guests are unassigned.

commands.name: app grant
commands.description: Owner-only grants. kind=app is a login on one App (host = the box login): a role, or Thread-only rooms. Since 0.45.5 a login needs the grant for that App and its pass reaches only that App's rooms. Other kinds store a scope and no role (recorded, not enforced). Revoke deletes the grant, keeps the role, and ends that App's live logins.

commands.name: app grant list
commands.description: List grants (subject, kind, target, role or scope). Owner only.

commands.name: app grant add
commands.usage: k2 app grant add --subject-kind principal|workspace --subject <id> --kind app|mailbox|database|cli|chat --target <id> [--role <role> | --room <handle>…] [--scope <text>]
commands.description: Create a grant. kind=app takes --role (role id or name) or --room (repeatable; Thread-only rooms, or --scope as a JSON array), not both; --target is host, a published service id, or <workspace>/<name> (unknown Apps 400). Other kinds require --scope and no --role. Principal subject is a principals.id. Workspace subject is a non-empty id (not looked up). kind=chat creates the Sew account (Sew must be enabled; Linux): --target optional (sew); principal --subject may be a username, scope member (default) or guest; workspace --subject may be a handle, scope coworker or assistant:<username|owner>. Roles and channels are set in Sew. Owner only.

commands.name: app grant rm
commands.description: Revoke a grant. The role stays. A kind=app grant's live logins on that App end.

commands.name: app grant set
commands.description: Change a chat grant's scope: member <-> guest, or re-pin an assistant. coworker <-> assistant is refused (delete and add again). Owner only.

commands.name: app grant hooks
commands.description: Grant hooks (Sew S27): status shows targets, outbox counts, blocked and held rows; log lists outbox rows (--subject <ext id>, --limit N); retry <id> re-arms a blocked row or a pending row that failed; skip <id> drops a blocked row and reconciles; reconcile sweeps now; target chat --on|--off [--socket P] [--token-file P]. The actor on a row is reported by K2, not proof a person acted. Owner only.

commands.name: app grant copy-host
commands.description: Give everyone who has the box login the same access on one App (their role when it is host-wide or that App's, else their rooms). A grant already on that App wins (even a disabled one); a role tagged for another App is skipped. Use after publishing an App (it starts with nobody) or before a BFF starts sending app on login. The owner copies at once; an agent's call (its own workspace's App) is one held request listing exactly the logins, approved by the owner from a card on its Thread or Settings → App Approvals (exit 2); the approval copies exactly those, or nothing if the list changed.

commands.name: app grant guests-rooms
commands.description: The owner; or the App's own agent in its own room with "Let this agent manage its Apps' users" (else, or another workspace's room, one held request with a card for the owner, exit 2) (RS-A15, 0.46.1; 0.46.4). Lets <app> read and set its OWN guests' rooms with its own App pass (GET|POST /cli/skin/guests/rooms; the server SDK's k2.asApp().guests.rooms / guests.setRooms), so its server never carries the owner token. It may hand out the --room rooms plus its own room, never a room above a guest's role, never the owner, Connect users or another App's guests. Granting again replaces the rooms. --revoke takes it back (an agent may revoke its own App's: it narrows). Audited (k2 app history).

commands.name: app guest rooms
commands.description: Read or set one guest's rooms on <app> (RS-A15). The owner acts with owner rights (any room); an agent acts on its own workspace's App only while the owner's guests-rooms grant stands, and only within it. Never above the guest's role (a role guest keeps its role's rooms). Idempotent (the same rooms are a no-op), 60 calls a minute per App, every change audited with before and after. Other Apps' guests and unknown names are the same not_found.

commands.name: app guest ceiling
commands.description: What <app> may hand its guests (app.rooms, 0.46.4): its own room, whether the owner granted guests-rooms, the grant's rooms and the ceiling guests.setRooms enforces (empty without the grant). The owner: any App; an agent: its own workspace's App. Reads only.

commands.name: app guest list
commands.description: <app>'s own guests by username with their rooms on it, role, on/off and agent mark (guests.list, 0.46.4). Never the owner, a Connect login or another App's guest. The owner: any App; an agent: its own workspace's App while the owner's guests-rooms grant stands. One page counts against the App's 60 calls a minute.

commands.name: app wallet
commands.usage: k2 app wallet settings <app> [--on|--off] [--fallback on|off] | people [<app>] | remove <item-id> | personal-agent <app> <user> <workspace> | personal-agent --clear <workspace> | personal-agents [--json]
commands.description: App users' personal wallets (0.46.3): each App user keeps their own LLM subscriptions and API keys from the App (wallet.* verbs); their subscription runs only their own personal agent. The owner (or an Admin) turns an App's wallet on, sets its fallback to the company plan, sees each item's existence, label and status (never a secret, link or code), force-removes (deleted, not Trash) and marks personal agents. An agent of the App's own workspace with switch 2 may set the fallback only. Each person's subscription runs only their own agent; check that your plan's terms allow the way your App uses it.

commands.name: app hydra
commands.description: OIDC issuer sidecar (Linux leftover). Still owner even when Agent-tab Apps is on.

commands.name: app front-door
commands.usage: k2 app front-door [connect|direct] [--url URL] [--hint TEXT] [--ui-port N] [--json]
commands.description: Optional Caddy path-filter (not required to host an app). Host the UI with k2 publish on any nested label; see k2 study apps.

commands.name: app token
commands.description: Mint/list/revoke platform k2skn_ capability passes (thread:read / thread:post / files:read / files:write). Secret shown once. List is platform-only (hides login sessions). Leftover: k2 skin-token.

commands.name: app token create
commands.description: Mint a platform k2skn_ pass. Name is a label (vercel), not a guest. Raw secret printed once. Default caps: thread:read + thread:post (never silent-add files).

commands.name: app token list
commands.description: List platform k2skn_ tokens (name + prefix + caps, never the secret). Hides login sessions.

commands.name: app token rooms
commands.description: Set rooms on a platform token. --clear empties rooms (Thread dark, keep secret).

commands.name: app token revoke
commands.description: Revoke a platform app pass. Next GET / overlay is 401.

commands.name: app members
commands.description: Who holds a grant on a room (room-scope R9): guests and agent logins with their role and caps, from grants, not presence. Connect logins are one line, admins of this box. Owner and admins: any room; an agent: its own room. GET /cli/app/members.

commands.name: app room-names
commands.description: Owner, outside K2: hide (or show) guests' names from Apps in that room's member list. The owner and Gardens still see them. POST /cli/app/room-names.

commands.name: app self
commands.description: An App's live Seed, health and when its live deployment went live (room-scope R16; an agent: its own workspace's Apps). GET /cli/app/self.

commands.name: app usage
commands.description: An App's quotas, live connections and per-call counts from its own audit (room-scope R16). GET /cli/app/usage.

commands.name: skin user add

commands.name: skin user email

commands.name: skin user password

commands.name: skin user unlock

commands.name: skin user rooms

commands.description: Create a skin role. --agent optional (0 = Thread dark). --caps optional (Thread-only). Name charset is the same as usernames; Connect owner/admin/member (and the retired viewer) are rejected.

commands.name: skin role list
commands.description: List skin roles (name + caps + rooms; no secrets).

commands.name: skin role update
commands.description: Update a role. --clear empties rooms, keeps caps. Always rewrites live sessions of assigned guests (never platform tokens).

commands.description: Owner/admin Remote Session surface: Layer 0 master switch, shell grants (k2rs_ token shown once), grant-bound shell PTY spawn, terminal write/read. Defaults OFF. Locked id tool.

commands.name: remote-session status

commands.name: remote-session enable

commands.description: Mint a shell grant. Prints k2rs_ token once (cannot be retrieved again). Mint allowed while Layer 0 is OFF; use blocked until enable.

commands.name: remote-session grants

commands.name: remote-session revoke

commands.name: wiki
commands.description: Per-workspace knowledge base (brain map) under .k2/wiki/: index graph, read notes, seed Home/_Index, localhost serve, publish via nested subdomain. Hosting is being rebuilt on the K2 runtime; public chat is unavailable.

commands.name: wiki status
commands.description: Local serve state (enabled/port/url) + published label + note count. publicChatEnabled is always false (chat unavailable).

commands.name: wiki index
commands.description: Full wiki graph index (nodes + wikilinks) from the daemon indexer.

commands.name: wiki note

commands.name: wiki seed
commands.description: Create seed Home.md + _Index.md under .k2/wiki/ when missing.

commands.name: wiki serve
commands.description: Start/stop the read-only localhost wiki site (binds 127.0.0.1 only).

commands.name: wiki chat
commands.description: Public chat is unavailable until it returns on the K2 runtime. `on` exits 3 (public_chat_unavailable); `off` turns it off.

commands.name: wiki publish
commands.description: Turn serve ON and create/point a nested subdomain to 127.0.0.1:port (or print the k2 publish subdomain command).

commands.name: wiki unpublish
commands.description: Turn serve OFF and print how to remove the nested subdomain (notes are kept).

commands.name: zen
commands.description: Build Zen Gardens on this computer (~/.k2/zen: gardens/<id>.toml, one page per Garden; zen.toml; themes/<name>/; widgets/<name>/ custom widgets; K2's built-in themes and templates are read-only defaults underneath) through the local daemon. Widgets in your own Gardens need no permissions. Exit 3 when Zen isn't set up here.

commands.name: zen garden
commands.description: The Gardens on this computer. list prints index, id, name and template (* = its own theme); new makes an empty Garden (--texting: the texting page) and prints its id and file; rename and reorder keep the id; template turns a Garden into the texting page (the default) or an empty one, same id, name and place, keeping the old file in .history/; delete moves the page into .history/ and exits 1 with "That's your last Garden." on the last one; lock and unlock are for the person only (agents exit 3), and a locked Garden refuses agent changes with exit 3 (garden_locked). access <garden> shows the Garden's list of agents who may edit it (or whether you may), ask asks the person, add|remove <agent> are the person's; history <garden> is its History (k2 study garden-access). <garden> is an id or a name.

commands.name: zen inspect
commands.description: Static review of a Garden bundle (zip) or folder you received, before anything is added: widgets and their caps/libs, every K2 verb called, network and escape attempts, URLs, obfuscation signals, parse and leak findings. Never runs the code. Everything quoted is untrusted, escaped and capped. Exit 0 report printed, 1 unreadable.

commands.name: zen widget errors
commands.usage: k2 zen widget errors <name> [--since <seq>] [--follow] [--json] | k2 zen widget errors <name> --clear [--all] [--json]
commands.description: Runtime errors your widget hit in a Zen window (uncaught errors and rejections, and bridge refusals such as not_bound), newest last, each with a suggestion and the version (bundle hash) that hit it. A refused sources.* call names its source address when a placement's config (or the manifest) names it; any other address is withheld. --follow keeps printing new ones. Each error says whether validate counts it (0.46.3): only a placed widget's errors on its saved version from the last 24 h count; the rest are marked old. --clear drops the ones that no longer count (an older version's, an unplaced widget's, older than 24 h), --clear --all every error; the person or any local agent, audited. Exit 0 none counted, 1 some (or the widget is unknown).

commands.name: zen validate
commands.description: Validate Zen files without changing what Zen shows: widget scripts are parsed (oxc) and linted (catalog, leaks); prints file:line:col: message per finding with a suggestion line. --dir checks a STAGED widget folder anywhere on disk (code as text, images/fonts too) exactly like a widget folder, and --garden <g> --from <file> a staged Garden page; neither writes anything. A check never signs (0.46.1): --widget --sign signs a clean version as the caller. Runtime errors (0.46.3) fail only for a widget a Garden places, on its saved version, from the last 24 h; an unplaced widget's or older ones are warnings (k2 zen widget errors <name> --clear drops them). With no target it reports each widget: where it is placed and its runtime state. Exit 0 ok (and 'pending': a placed widget whose saved version has not run in a Zen window yet), 1 errors (including a placed widget's recent runtime errors), 2 usage or, with --strict, pending or old runtime errors, 3 Zen not set up / Garden locked.

commands.name: zen widget delete
commands.description: Delete a custom widget that no Garden places (0.46.5). While any Garden places it, K2 refuses with widget_placed and names those Gardens (exit 1): take it off each Garden's page first. Its code is kept as a history snapshot and the whole folder (images, fonts) beside it; the answer prints the undo, k2 zen reset --widget <name> --to <snapshot>. Its data and last good version stay. The person, or an agent with "Manage Gardens and data sources" (Garden access on: as for put; a widget placed nowhere is open); any other agent gets person_only (exit 3). K2's built-in widgets can't be deleted. Exit 0 deleted, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 not allowed / Zen not set up, 4 no such widget.

commands.name: zen widget put
commands.usage: k2 zen widget put <name> <file> --from <path>|- [--note "…"] [--json] | k2 zen widget put [<name>] --dir <folder> [--prune] [--note "…"] [--json]
commands.description: Change a custom widget through K2 from anywhere on disk (never edit ~/.k2 yourself). One code file (.html .js .css .json; written even if the widget then has errors, the last good version keeps running), or with --dir the whole staged folder (code, images, .woff2 fonts) in one checked write: a folder with errors is refused and nothing is written; files the folder lacks are left alone unless --prune. The person, or an agent on the list of every Garden that places the widget, writes (in the Garden's History); any other agent is refused with garden_access_needed (exit 3) and K2 asks the person with a garden.access card. Nothing is proposed (proposals are retired: k2 study garden-changes). K2's built-in widgets are never written. k2 zen widget apply --from <folder> is the same as put --dir. Exit 0 written, 1 refused, 2 usage, 3 not on the Garden's list / locked / Zen not set up, 4 no such widget.

commands.name: zen widget preview
commands.usage: k2 zen widget preview --dir <folder> [<name>] [--config key=value]... [--json] | k2 zen widget preview --dir <folder> [<name>] --shot <png> [--theme dark|light] [--width N] [--height N] [--zen-theme <name>] [--data <file.json>] [--libs <dir>] [--wait-ms N] [--config key=value]... [--json] | k2 zen widget preview --clear [--json]
commands.description: Try a staged widget folder in Zen without touching the person's Gardens: K2 writes it as widgets/preview-<name>/ (manifest id renamed) and places it alone on K2's own "Widget preview" Garden (made the first time; each preview replaces the last). --config sets the placement's config (a card that reads data sources takes sources=a,b). It has its own empty store; its runtime errors are k2 zen widget errors preview-<name>. --clear removes the preview Garden and every preview-* widget. The person, or any agent in a K2 terminal (it never touches the person's Gardens). --shot <png> (0.46.3) renders the folder headless instead, with nobody at a Zen window: checked and bundled as Zen would, in K2's real widget frame on a Garden canvas, its calls answered by a stand-in bridge with sample data (or --data fixtures), drawn in WebKit at 2x; it writes only the PNG, any local agent may shoot, and Zen needn't be set up. Needs Node.js and Playwright's WebKit (npm install -g playwright && npx playwright install webkit). Exit 0 previewed, cleared or shot (the widget said ready), 1 refused (errors) or the shot widget threw / never said ready (PNG still written), 2 usage, 3 needs a person / Zen not set up / no Node or Playwright WebKit.

commands.name: zen reload
commands.description: Re-read ~/.k2/zen now (the daemon also watches it) and print current errors.

commands.name: zen reset
commands.description: Keep the current file as a snapshot, then restore a snapshot or clear your changes (a Garden goes back to its template's stub; an override of a built-in theme is removed; --widget restores a widget's code files, never its assets). Never touches gardens.json, active.json or widget grants.

commands.name: zen history
commands.description: The last 20 good versions of each Zen file, newest first, including deleted Gardens (by id).

commands.name: zen doctor
commands.description: Check the Zen folder, Garden list, templates, files, watcher and history on this computer.

commands.name: zen theme
commands.description: The active Zen theme (one for this computer, plus an optional pick per Garden). list shows K2's built-in themes and yours; next/prev cycle them; set picks one (exit 1 and the list on an unknown name); new copies a theme into ~/.k2/zen/themes/<name>/ to edit.

commands.name: zen widget
commands.description: Custom widgets: your own sealed HTML, CSS and JS in ~/.k2/zen/widgets/<name>/, placed with [[widget]] kind = "custom". new copies a working example and prints the folder (409 widget_exists if it's there); list shows each widget's state, caps and every placement (and whether the runaway guard paused its posting); show <name> adds the caps it runs with, the reach note (0.46.1: a widget that reads sources keeps thread:post and store:write when its manifest asks for them) and the source addresses each placement reads; errors <name> [--since <seq>] [--follow] lists its runtime errors (class, code and line only for a widget that reads data sources). A widget in your own Garden can talk to your agents right away: no grant, no review. k2 zen widget grant and revoke only say so. The helpers a widget can call: k2 zen guide api.

commands.name: zen path
commands.description: Print the Zen folder (~/.k2/zen on the daemon's computer).

commands.name: zen sync
commands.usage: k2 zen sync [--json] | k2 zen sync <garden> on|off|preview|undo|keep-previous [--page|--theme] [--json]
commands.description: Whether each Garden's page and theme sync with K2's defaults or are its own copy (prd-zen-garden-sync-defaults-v1). No arguments: every Garden's state, its own changes and whether K2's default changed since its copy. on/off/undo/keep-previous are the person's (an agent gets 403 zen_local_only: ask the person, Settings → Gardens); preview prints the Garden as if synced and writes nothing.

commands.name: zen links
commands.usage: k2 zen links [<garden>] [--json] | k2 zen links forget <garden> <site>
commands.description: The sites each Garden opens in the person's browser without asking (k2.open from a widget, 0.46.4): the person chose Always on K2's own card. Agents can read the list; only the person changes it (forget is refused inside a K2 terminal: run it outside K2).

commands.name: zen news
commands.usage: k2 zen news [--json] | k2 zen news seen [<id>... | --all] [--json]
commands.description: Unseen Garden news (new catalog Gardens; K2 defaults a synced Garden picked up; notices of a one-time change K2 made, like 0.46.4 moving the data cards to @3 and listing the Gardens it left) and how many own copies have a newer default. seen marks ids, or every unseen item with --all, as read.

commands.name: zen agents-order
commands.description: The person's order and pins in each Garden's Agents widget on this computer (they drag rows and pin agents in Zen; per Garden, never synced). Read only: agents can read it and never set it. order sits on top of the widget's own order; pins, once set, replace the agents' workspace pins in that Garden's pin grid.

commands.name: zen guide
commands.usage: k2 zen guide [<topic>] [--json] | k2 zen guide example [<name> [--toml] | --list] [--json]
commands.description: The Zen Gardens user guide: short static pages (gardens, files, widgets, bands, required, menus, themes, sync, examples, undo, safe-mode, api), each at most 80 lines, and whole example Garden files (rail-top, quiet-top, bottom-bar, menu-both, texting-chrome, menu-bottom-right, column-corner). Daemon-optional. An unknown topic or example exits 2.

commands.name: skills
commands.description: Manage skill profiles (SKILL.md) for workspaces/agents.

commands.name: settings
commands.description: Show this workspace's settings (name, mode, heartbeat, pinned), or set its mode with --mode off|custom|manager|k2. A daemon refusal exits 3.

commands.name: version
commands.description: Print the CLI version.

commands.name: --schema

commands.name: study

help.compute:
k2 compute — run commands on your own machines (compute nodes)

Agents:
  k2 compute nodes [--json]                  nodes granted to this workspace
  k2 compute status [--json]                 every node at a glance: state, waits
                 (foreign locks), run/queue and the jobs, free CPU/mem, load,
                 disk free vs floor; plus this controller (disk, Time Machine
                 local snapshots). Hand-run lock files, cache sizes and pinned
                 long-runners need node reporting, which nodes don't send yet.
                 (k2 compute status <job> is get)
  k2 compute info <node> [--json]
  k2 compute run <node>|--any [--os linux] [--arch x86_64] [--label k=v]
                 [--detach] [--dirty] [--sha REV] [--no-source]
                 [--env K=V]... [--cpus N] [--mem 16G]
                 [--secret NAME[=ENVNAME]]...  a vault secret as env, sealed to the
                                node at spawn; names only in the plan (k2 study compute)
                 [--timeout D (≤ the grant's max, default 2h; k2 compute nodes shows it)]
                 [--exclusive] [--retry-interrupted|--no-retry] [--raw] [--workspace WS]
                 [--wait [--failures] [--max-wait 9m]]
                 [--artifact GLOB]... [--json]
                 [--queue-timeout 30m|off] [--retries N] [--stall-timeout 30m|off]
                 [--shards N]   (with --any: N jobs, {shard}/{shards} in the command)
                 [--tier ci|priority|normal]   queue order on the node (never stops a running job)
                      ci        highest; next free slot (needs a grant with --ci; release and CI runs)
                      priority  the critical path: next free slot after CI. One submitter per server at
                                a time (a courtesy: K2 doesn't stop you, it prints a note). Optional:
                                use it only when one result blocks others; independent work stays Normal.
                      normal    default; first come, first served in a workspace; workspaces take turns
                 [--gate]       = --tier ci (kept for scripts)   [--critical] = --tier priority
                 [--supersede KEY]   cancel your older QUEUED jobs with the same KEY (never a running one)
                 [--submitter NAME]  name this submitter (display and the Priority note; not security)
                 [--plan]     dry run: the node it would pick, queue, warm slot,
                                estimate from earlier runs, grant left (JSON)
                 [--needs node@22,python@3.12,rust@stable,cargo-nextest,cmake@3,sys:pkg-config]
                 (tools: node python go java bun deno zig cmake ninja protoc uv pnpm,
                  rust@<ch>, cargo-nextest, sys:<pkg>, or aqua:owner/repo@v;
                  anything else is refused: tool_unsupported, exit 2)
                 -- <command…>
  k2 compute test [<node>|--any] [--shards N] [run flags] [-- <nextest args>]
                 a cargo-nextest suite split across nodes (nextest --partition),
                 JUnit kept and parsed, one combined result; --profile P to use
                 the repo's own nextest profile, --runner to replace cargo nextest run
  k2 compute jobs [--node N] [--mine] [--state S] [--tier T] [--limit N] [--workspace WS] [--json]
                 From a git worktree inside the workspace (.claude/worktrees/x) the
                 workspace is found for you, and run takes HEAD and --dirty from
                 that worktree; from anywhere else pass --workspace <handle>.
  k2 compute get <job> [--json]              --json: the result (exit, duration, node,
                                             artifacts + sha256, tests, receipt id)
  k2 compute fetch <job> [NAME...] [--out DIR] [--json] [--over-relay]
                                             copy kept artifacts here (all, or NAMEs);
                                             --over-relay: files over 100 MB through
                                             the relay too (up to 500 MB)
  k2 compute wait <job>... [--failures] [--max-wait 9m] [--quiet] [--json]
                 block until the jobs end, no log text; exit = the job's exit
                 code (first failing job for several), 3 for cancelled/failed/
                 timeout, 3 + still_running when --max-wait passes first.
                 run --wait = submit, print the id, then wait (no [compute]
                 message while it waits; a --detach job always gets one).
  k2 compute attach <job> [--since SEQ] [--raw]
  k2 compute logs <job> [--tail N] [--failures] [--raw]
                                             --failures: failing tests first, then log lines
  k2 compute cancel <job> [--force]
                 a queued job is cancelled at once; one that already started
                 (or was just assigned) needs --force (else job_started, exit 3).
                 On a shared node, a job in the node's queue is asked to cancel
                 only if it hasn't started: it ends cancelled, or job_started
  k2 compute queue <node> [--json]
                 the node's whole queue: on a shared node, other servers' jobs
                 show only as "another server" with tier, class, size and ETA
  k2 compute retry <job>
  k2 compute receipt <job>
Owner / admin (refused for agents and inside K2 terminals, except where
"Allow managing compute nodes" is on for that agent: see k2 compute manage):
  k2 compute preview on|off|status             turn the preview on for this server (owner)
  k2 compute node add <name> [--url URL]       mint a 10-minute enroll code
  k2 compute node confirm <name> <code>        the 6 digits the node shows
  k2 compute node remove <name>                k2 compute node rename <old> <new>
  k2 compute node retire <name>                drain, then remove once its jobs end
  k2 compute node pause|drain|resume <name>    this server stops/starts assigning
  k2 compute node route add|rm <name> <url>    LAN or tailnet URL the node may dial
Sharing a node with other K2 servers (the node's owner server; 0.46.3):
  k2 compute node servers <node> [--json]      every server on it: slot, state,
                   trust, share, today's use, end date, pending SAS
  k2 compute node servers <node> add --url URL --code CODE.FP [--trust own|team]
                   [--for 7d|none] [--weight N] [--max-running N] [--max-queued N]
                   [--cpu-hours N] [--max-time 2h] [--cpus N] [--mem 8G]
                   [--disk 40G] [--network on|no-lan|none] [--gate] [--exclusive]
                   CODE.FP is what `k2 compute node add <node>` printed on the
                   NEW server. Held for your approval (Touch ID / vault
                   password); the new server's owner then confirms the SAS.
                   Needs the node's remote-admin level `full`; on a node set
                   to `policy`, add servers at the machine instead:
                   sudo k2-node servers add --url URL --code CODE.FP
  k2 compute node servers <node> approve|deny <request>   (= node admin approve/deny)
  k2 compute node servers <node> limits <server> [--weight N] key=value…
                   narrowing at once, widening (a higher weight too) waits
                   for approval (max_running, max_queued, cpu_hours_day,
                   max_job_secs, max_cpus, max_mem_gb, disk_gb, weight,
                   network, top_class, gate, exclusive; for=7d|none;
                   priority=true|false: its --tier priority counts here, a
                   0.46.5 node only; true is a widening). Every server
                   starts at weight 1, the owner too; <server> may be
                   slot:0 (this server) for its weight
  k2 compute node servers <node> pause|resume <server>
  k2 compute node servers <node> revoke <server> [--now] [--wipe]   (owner)
  k2 compute node servers <node> owner <server> [--old keep|revoke]
                   [--caches move|wipe] [--now] [--reason TEXT]   (owner, 0.46.4)
                   make another of your own servers on the node its owner
                   (active, confirmed, online). Held for your approval; the
                   node drains (--now stops running jobs), the two swap
                   slots and root re-pins to the new owner. This server
                   stays as one of your servers, with a new server's
                   default share (--old revoke: it leaves, its queued jobs
                   end share_revoked, its files go after 24 h); caches move
                   with their server (or --caches wipe). Before approving,
                   check the full key on the card against the new owner's
                   controllerFp (k2 compute nodes --json there). Needs
                   remote admin `full`; else at the machine:
                   sudo k2-node servers owner <server> --fp <full key>
  k2 compute node take-owner <node>   (owner, in person; 0.46.4)
                   a node another of your servers made this server's owner:
                   it says so, but stays that server's here until you take
                   it over. It shows the node's full key, the old owner and
                   every compute:<ws>/* secret grant that starts reaching
                   it; you type the node's name, then Touch ID / vault
                   password. An offer alone never makes a node this server's.
  k2 compute grant <node> --workspace WS [--max-time 2h] [--max-disk 60G]
                   [--max-parallel 1] [--max-queued 10] [--ci|--no-ci]
                   --ci: this workspace may send --tier ci (it jumps every queue;
                   owner or an Admin login only; absent keeps what it was)
  k2 compute revoke <node> --workspace WS
  k2 compute grants [--node N] [--workspace WS]
  k2 compute access on|off --workspace WS
                   the Agent tab's "Allow compute nodes" (Settings → Workspaces →
                   <agent> → Agent): on = a grant on every machine switched on,
                   default limits (and ones added later); off removes them all
  k2 compute usage [--days N]    k2 compute events [--limit N]
Node admin (agents need "Allow this agent to operate compute nodes"):
  k2 compute node health <node> [--json]       uptime, disk, RAM, FileVault, update state
  k2 compute node policy <node> show
  k2 compute node policy <node> set key=value... [--reason "…"]
                   narrowing applies at once; widening waits for the owner (exit 2)
  k2 compute node update <node> [--canary] [--now]   offer the signed k2-node build
  k2 compute node rollback <node> [--now]      back to the node's own previous build
                   a shared node first waits for running jobs (up to 30 min);
                   --now skips the wait. Solo nodes never wait. Nodes on 0.46.3
                   or older need one manual install of 0.46.4 first (their
                   updater can't run the new build): sudo k2-node setup
  k2 compute node wall <node> [--no-restart] [--reason "…"]
                   Linux: turn the job wall on (jobs run as k2job, walled off
                   from the node's key, /home and /root). At once on 0.46.4+
                   nodes at remote admin policy; k2-node restarts to use it once
                   its running jobs end, only if this call changed the wall's
                   files; after 30 min with jobs still running it gives up and
                   restarts nothing (--no-restart: at the next restart). An
                   older node, a node whose owner ran setup --no-job-wall, or
                   one with its own job user holds it for the owner (exit 2)
  k2 compute node admin propose <node> <verb> [key=value…] --reason "…"
                   verbs today: unit.restart unit=k2-node [now=true], policy.set key=value,
                   control.pause|drain|resume, gc, jobs.kill job_id=…,
                   wall.enable [restart=true] (Linux: jobs run as k2job; or k2 compute node wall),
                   homes.private (chmod 700 the homes others can read)
  k2 compute node admin propose <node> --plan plan.json --reason "…"
                   held for the owner: exit 2 with the request id
  k2 compute node admin list [--node N] [--state open|pending|all] [--json]
  k2 compute node admin withdraw <id>
Node admin, owner only (refused for agents and inside K2 terminals):
  k2 compute node admin approve <id>           Touch ID / your password, then signed + sent
  k2 compute node admin deny <id> [--why "…"]
  k2 compute node alerts <node> [--after 10m|off]   offline alert after N minutes
  k2 compute node alerts --to <workspace>|none      where alerts go (an IT agent)
  k2 compute operate on|off --workspace WS
                   the Agent switch "Allow this agent to operate compute nodes"
  k2 compute manage on|off --workspace WS      (owner only)
                   the Agent switch "Allow managing compute nodes": that agent may
                   node add/confirm/rename/pause/drain/resume/retire/route and
                   grant/revoke any workspace (each act in Access Audit). Still
                   yours: preview on|off, node remove, and this switch
This computer (its owner):
  k2 compute local status|pause [--now]|drain|resume
  k2 compute local policy key=value...    (cpu_cap_percent, mem_cap_gb, availability, …)
  k2 compute local enable [--controller URL --enroll CODE.FP --name NAME]
                          [--private-home | --no-private-home]
                          [--remote-admin off|policy|full]   (default policy:
                          K2 keeps this node updated and healthy; full also
                          lets it run root actions, each approved by you)
  k2 compute local remote-admin off|policy|full   change it later (root: one
                          sudo or admin prompt; off = K2 can't update the node).
                          Only the owner: this machine's K2, or the owner
                          signed in over K2 Connect; never an agent
  k2 compute local disable [--yes]   lists the jobs running here first; with
                          jobs running it asks (or needs --yes): they stop now

Never stuck: a job that can't start within --queue-timeout (default 30m
attached, 24h --detach) fails with queue_timeout; --any jobs move off a node
that sleeps or is paused; infrastructure failures (node lost, sync, spawn)
retry --retries times (default 1) with backoff, on another node when --any.
A job that prints nothing for --stall-timeout (default 30m) ends as
timeout/stalled. A non-zero exit, a timeout, a stall or a cancel is a
result and never retried.
Exit codes: 0–255 = the command's own exit (attached runs); 2 = bad usage;
3 = infra, with a JSON code on stderr (node_offline, not_granted,
compute_off, queue_full, owner_only, job_started, …); 130 = you detached
with Ctrl-C (the job keeps running). run --json prints one result object
on stdout (logs go to stderr). Jobs see K2_COMPUTE_JOB=<id> (set by the
node; the only K2_* variable in a job). --secret: the job gets a vault
secret as env; only a person grants it (k2 vault grant NAME --to
compute:<ws>/<node> --as env), and the job can print or send what it's
given. Read `k2 study compute` first.
help.sidecar:
k2 sidecar — open extra AI sessions (sidecars) in a workspace

  k2 sidecar new <name> --harness <preset> [--brief <file>|-] [--brief-text "…"]
                 [--workspace <ws>] [--model <model>] [--json]
  k2 sidecar list [--workspace <ws>] [--json]
  k2 sidecar stop <name> [--workspace <ws>] [--force] [--json]
  k2 sidecar access on|off|status [--workspace <ws>]      owner/admin

A sidecar shares this workspace's role, skills and inbox. Its address is
<workspace>/<name>. Message it with k2 msg <address>; it replies the same way.
new on a stopped name resumes the same conversation.
Harnesses: claude, grok, codex, gemini, cursor-agent, pi, hermes (any preset that runs them).
Agents: only the main session, only with "Allow hiring and managing agents" on.
Do not put secrets in a brief.
More: k2 study sidecars
help.vault:
k2 vault — secrets for agents, without showing them the value

  k2 vault status                          where the key lives, recovery, honest line
  k2 vault list [--scope <s>] [--system]   names, scope, sites, delivery (never values)
  k2 vault show NAME [--scope <s>]         one secret: sites, delivery, shares, recent use
  k2 vault set NAME [options] < value      create, or a new version (value on stdin)
  k2 vault rotate NAME < value             a new version
  k2 vault hosts NAME --add <host> | --remove <host>
  k2 vault delivery NAME fetch|agent|file|env|api [--ceiling <d>]
                                           (no --env-name here: names live on grants)
  k2 vault sign NAME ovh|hmac-sha256|hmac-sha256-ts|none [--sign-header …]
                                           K2 signs fetch requests with the secret
  k2 vault public-key NAME                 an ssh key's .pub line (never the private key)
  k2 vault agent-limit NAME [--burst N] [--per-minute M] [--allow-forwarded|--no-forwarded]
                                           an ssh key's agent signing limits (agent delivery)
  k2 vault grant NAME --to ws:<name>|ws:*|session:<id>|service:<label>|job:<name>|compute:<ws>/<node> [--as <d>] [--env-name X]
  k2 vault revoke NAME --from <who>        (or --grant <id>)
  k2 vault disable|enable NAME             destroy NAME --yes
  k2 vault fetch --secret NAME [-X M] [-H 'N: v'] [-d @file] URL
                                           K2 makes the call and adds the key; you never see it
  k2 vault get NAME                        print a value (needs an api grant; it lands in your transcript)
  k2 vault audit [NAME] [--since <rfc3339>]
  k2 vault requests                        Thread secret cards (pending / set / declined)
  k2 vault presets                         known key formats (Stripe, OpenAI, Anthropic, …)
  k2 vault env-file --secret NAME [--ttl 60]   a short-lived 0600 file for docker/podman --env-file
  k2 vault import .env [--scope <s>] [--remove-original]   move a .env in; writes .env.k2 (references)
  k2 vault service <service> [clean|legacy] [--env-file .env.k2]   a published service's environment
  k2 publish secret add|remove|list <service> NAME [--as file|env]   secrets a service gets at start
  k2 vault doctor                          plaintext .env files, due rotations, problems
  k2 vault send NAME --to <agent>[::<host>] [--note …]   hand a secret to another agent by name
  k2 vault incoming | sent | accept-from   handoffs to and from this agent (k2 vault send --help)
  k2 vault placement add NAME --where <host>:<path> [--note …] | done ID | rm ID
                                           note a place the value lives that K2 doesn't write
  k2 vault placements [NAME]               where values live outside the vault (due after a rotate)

  People only (from your own terminal or SSH, not a K2 terminal):
  k2 vault reveal NAME                     show a value (asks for a confirm)
  k2 vault recovery show-once              make and show the recovery key once; type back 3 words
  k2 vault recovery rotate                 replace the recovery key (asks for a confirm)
  k2 vault confirm-password set            set the vault password used for confirms
  k2 vault kek rotate | rekey              rotate the box key / the data key (owner, confirm)
  k2 vault rollback NAME --to <version>    put an older version back (confirm)
  k2 vault systemd-cred NAME --unit <unit.service> [--restart] [--dry-run] | --remove
                                           seal it as a root unit's systemd credential (Linux, confirm)
  k2 vault systemd-cred NAME --replace     re-place a new version into its root units (confirm)
  k2 vault backup <dir>                    a ciphertext snapshot of the vault (owner)
  k2 vault backup key <age1…>              also let this backup key open the vault (owner)
  k2 vault restore --from <dir> [--holder recovery|backup] [--dry-run] [--replace]
                                           restore a backup on this box (recovery words or backup key on stdin)

  Moving secrets to another box (owner, Admin, or an agent allowed to manage server-wide secrets):
  k2 vault recipient                       this vault's carry address (run it on the target box)
  k2 vault carry export --recipient <age1…> --target <vault-id> --workspace <ws> [--target-workspace <id>] [--server NAME] [--own-box-move] --out <file>
  k2 vault carry import <file> [--workspace <id>] [--apply]
                                           lists first (with the target workspace id); --apply puts them in this box's vault.
                                           Workspace secrets match by id, never by name: --workspace <id> on this box, or the
                                           id the carry was made for (--target-workspace). A name works only if it is that id.

Scope (--scope): ws:<workspace> (default inside a workspace), server, session.
set options:
  --kind api_key|password|oauth_token|ssh_key|tls_key|dsn|url|generic   (default api_key)
  --for <host>[,<host>]       sites this secret may be sent to (exact hosts)
  --preset stripe|openai|anthropic|xai|gemini|github|slack|supabase|ovh-eu|ovh-ca|ovh-us
                              fills the sites and where the key goes in a request
  --sign ovh|hmac-sha256|hmac-sha256-ts [--sign-header <Name> …]
                              K2 signs each request instead (k2 vault set --help)
  --inject-dst header:<Name>|query:<param>|basic|body   where fetch puts the key
  --inject-header <Name>      same as --inject-dst header:<Name>
  --inject-format '<fmt>'     how it's written, one {} (e.g. 'Bearer {}'; default {})
  --delivery fetch|agent|file|env|api   how agents get it (default fetch for keys;
                              agent: ssh keys sign on $SSH_AUTH_SOCK, never shown)
  --ceiling fetch|agent|file|env|api    the loosest delivery allowed later
  --describe <text>  --rotate-every <days>  --ttl <secs> (session scope)

Where the key goes is fixed by whoever creates the secret (header and
format); agents name the secret and K2 adds it. The presets fill this in
for common key formats, so you usually just confirm.

Agents: use `k2 vault fetch` (K2 makes the call and adds the key), never
paste a key into a file or chat; ask a person with `k2 thread secret`.
Each verb has its own help: k2 vault <verb> --help.
More: k2 study vault
help.job:
k2 job — scheduled jobs the K2 daemon runs (no session, no LLM, no cron)

  k2 job add NAME (--every 15m | --cron '*/15 * * * *') [--timeout 10m]
             [--cwd <dir>] -- <cmd> [args…]
  k2 job edit NAME [--every …|--cron …] [--timeout …] [--cwd …] [-- <cmd> …]
  k2 job list [--all] [--json]          show NAME [--json]
  k2 job logs NAME [--run ID] [--json]  run NAME (same: run-now)
  k2 job enable|disable NAME            (same: resume|pause NAME)
  k2 job kill NAME                      stop the run in progress
  k2 job rm NAME                        remove it and its secret grants
  k2 job pause --all | resume --all     every job (owner or admin only)
  --workspace <name>                    people: which workspace (default:
                                        the one this folder is in)

Each run gets its own K2 identity (k2 vault fetch, k2 db dsn and k2 msg
work as in a K2 tab), only the secrets granted to job:NAME
(k2 vault grant KEY --to job:NAME --as env|file|agent|fetch), the workspace
folder as its working folder, and a PATH with k2 on it. No shell unless
you write one: -- sh -c '…'. Runs never overlap. The timeout (default
10m, max 6h) stops the whole process group. Logs are redacted
([k2v:NAME]) and capped at 1 MiB; the last 20 are kept.
Agents may add jobs in their own workspace; each add, edit and removal
posts a line on the workspace's Thread.
More: k2 study jobs

study.title: What K2 is
study.summary: What this product is (agents as infrastructure)
study.body:
k2 study what — what this product is

K2 is agent server software. Not an IDE. Not a model provider. Not a
wrapper SDK. You host a team of agents on your machine; they keep
working when the window closes.

WHAT YOU GET
  - Named workspaces, each with one primary agent (and optional sidecars)
  - A local daemon that owns sessions, inboxes, and the CLI
  - Humans on the same box (or via Connect) watching live terminals
  - Agents that message each other without you as the relay
  - Any terminal coding agent you already pay for (Claude, Codex, Grok, …)
  - Always-on context composed once; load skills for depth
  - Optional mail and loopback Postgres sidecars your human enables

WHAT K2 IS NOT
  - Not a hosted model. Bring your own keys / subscriptions.
  - Not MIT-licensed SaaS. Source-available Fair Source — see `k2 study source`.
  - Not K2 Connect. Connect is a separate product (tunnel + account).
    The app, daemon, and CLI live in the K2 repo. See `k2 study connect-boundary`.
  - Not a dump of this workspace's wiki, PRDs, or release runbooks.

HOW YOU DRIVE IT
  The `k2` CLI is the agent interface. `k2 help` lists verbs (needs a
  daemon). `k2 --schema` is the machine manifest (daemon-optional).
  `k2 study` is these bounded pages — concepts, not a flag dump.
  Load the k2-cli skill for the command reference.

WHO YOU TALK TO
  Humans: `k2 thread` in this chat, `k2 feedback ask` for a durable
  question. Other agents: `k2 msg`. Real email: `k2 mail`.
  Four people lists exist — never `k2 msg` usernames. See `k2 study people`.

WHEN SOMETHING IS REFUSED
  Exit 3 with owner_only / gated / forbidden means stop looping and ask
  your human. See `k2 study errors`. Do not treat a teaching refusal as
  "invalid token" and retry.

RELATED PAGES
  source · map · identity · send · people · errors · connect-boundary

K2 is source-available Fair Source, not MIT. To change this box, `k2 feedback ask` with a brief (`k2 study ticket-brief`). To talk in this chat, `k2 thread`.

study.title: License and repo boundary
study.summary: License + repo boundary (Fair Source, not MIT)
study.body:
k2 study source — license + repo boundary

LICENSE
  K2 is Fair Source: FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 (Functional Source License).
  It is source-available. It is not MIT. It is not a permissive
  "do anything, including competing hosted clones" license.

  Free for personal and internal / business use. Each release converts
  to Apache 2.0 two years after that release. Competing commercial
  hosting of K2 is not a Permitted Purpose under FSL.

  Third-party MIT assets (for example a file-icon font) do not relicense
  the product. K2 code remains FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0.

WHAT LIVES IN THIS REPO
  - The K2 app (desktop UI)
  - The K2 daemon (always-on runtime)
  - The `k2` CLI (this command)
  - Workspace compose (AGENTS.md, skills, inboxes, db/mail sidecars)

WHAT DOES NOT
  K2 Connect — the control plane for purchased hostnames, accounts,
  and nested labels — is a separate product. Pairing
  (`k2 connect login`) talks to that plane; it is not "the daemon
  with a public IP". See `k2 study connect-boundary`.

  Do not treat GitHub wiki, this workspace's notes, or PRDs as the
  license. The license text ships as LICENSE.md in the K2 repo.
  NOTICE.md is the trademark + third-party map, not a second license.

COMMERCIAL HOSTING
  Official Connect is the intended multi-tenant remote-access path.
  Air-gapped / LAN-only daemon hosting is not the same grant — that
  needs a written Enterprise agreement. Do not invent a hosting
  story from CLI flags.

TRADEMARKS
  "K2" is the product name. Do not call it K2SO. The license does not
  grant trademark rights.

IF YOU WANT THIS BOX TO CHANGE
  You do not patch license policy from an agent session. File a
  durable ask: `k2 feedback ask`. To talk here: `k2 thread`.

k2 study map — how the surface is organized

PAGES, NOT VERBS
  `k2 help` is the verb list (needs the daemon). `k2 --schema` is the
  machine manifest (daemon-optional). `k2 study` is bounded concept
  pages. Do not treat study as a second --help, and do not crawl
  `.k2/wiki/` or `.k2/prds/` for product truth.

JOB → WHERE
  Who am I?                         k2 whoami          study identity
  Talk to another agent             k2 msg             study send
  Receive a file package            k2 inbox           study send
  Talk to the human in this chat    k2 thread          study human
  Durable question / approval       k2 feedback ask    study feedback-loop
  Real email                        k2 mail            study mail
  Workspace SQL                     k2 db / k2 store   study db
  Always-on context                 k2 agent context   study context
  Connected agent peers             k2 connections     study people
  Humans on this box                k2 connections list --users
  Connect-user accounts             k2 users           study people
  App guests                        k2 app user list   study apps
  Pair a purchased hostname         k2 connect         study connect-boundary
  Nested hostname for a port        k2 publish         study connect-boundary
  License / repo boundary           k2 study source
  Exit codes                        k2 study errors
  Identity / gates                  k2 study auth

HOW TO READ HELP
  `k2 help`           daily verbs (needs daemon)
  `k2 help <verb>`    one verb's flags
  `k2 help --advanced` heartbeats, daemon, publish, …
  `k2 --schema`       JSON surface for agents
  Study pages teach the why; help teaches the flags. Do not reprint
  --help here.

NOT ON THIS MAP (later)
  Heartbeats, presets, hire, API cells — use `k2 help --advanced` /
  per-verb help when the daemon is up. Study v1 does not replace them.

DAEMON-OPTIONAL
  `k2 study` and `k2 --schema` work with no heartbeat.port / token.
  Live unknown verbs do not. `k2 help` does not skip that gate.

K2 is source-available Fair Source, not MIT. To change this box, `k2 feedback ask` with a brief (`k2 study ticket-brief`). To talk in this chat, `k2 thread`.

study.title: Who you are
study.summary: Who you are; handles vs names; sidecars
study.body:
k2 study identity — who you are

`k2 whoami` prints this cell: workspace handle, role (canonical or
sidecar), address, primary, session. Facts, not a wake protocol.
You do not need to run it every turn.

CANONICAL VS SIDECAR
  canonical  — the workspace agent (primary).
  sidecar    — an extra chat in the same workspace (same role / inbox).
               Not a second agent. Owner messages in this chat stay here;
               do not forward them to primary unless asked.

ADDRESSES ARE HANDLES
  Use the handle from `k2 connections list` (`sales-team`), never the
  display name (`Sales Team`). Bare `k2 msg sales` is the primary.
  Sidecar: slash `sales/reviewer` or `sales/1`. Hyphen `sales-reviewer`
  is a workspace handle, not a sidecar.

HANDLES ARE NEVER REUSED
  A handle belongs to one workspace for good. After a rename the old
  handle still reaches the same workspace. After a workspace is removed
  its handles are retired: `k2 msg <retired>` fails and a new workspace
  gets `<name>-2`. Display names stay free to change and reuse.
  A federated connection follows the workspace, not the name: if that
  workspace leaves the other host, sends fail with
  `remote_workspace_gone` (never redirected to a new workspace with that
  name) until your human adds the connection again.

WHEN A CHAT IS RENAMED
  A sidecar's address follows its Chats name: `sales/3` renamed
  "Reviewer" answers at `sales/reviewer`. Old addresses keep working:
  `sales/3` (the number never changes) and every earlier name still
  reach the same chat; the CLI prints `note: sales/3 is now
  sales/reviewer`. Old names stay reserved to their chat until it is
  archived or someone runs Release old names in Chats. All-digit names
  are display only; `sales/3` is always the number. A live chat gets a
  `[k2] This chat's address is now …` line when it is renamed.

STAMPS YOU WILL SEE
  [thread:<addr>]    human wrote on the Thread tab → `k2 thread`
  [project:<name>]   project shared chat → `k2 project msg <name>`
  [inbox:<id>]       tray package → `k2 inbox read <id>`
  [from <name>]      another agent labeled a live msg

WHO IS NOT AN ADDRESS
  Connect-user names, Skin guests, and `--users` humans are not
  `k2 msg` targets. See `k2 study people`.

YOUR PICTURE AND COLOR
  `k2 agent identity` shows how you look. `k2 agent identity --color
  '#22c55e' --image me.png` (or --clear-image) changes your own look;
  every client updates live. Yours only: naming another agent is
  refused. Your name and handle are your owner's to change; ask them.

SESSION ROLE
  This CLI may run inside a scoped agent cell (passport in env) or
  from a human terminal. ID/locked tools need the session passport
  in-cell. Open tools (including `k2 study`) do not mint authority.
  See `k2 study auth`.

FEDERATED SHAPE
  Live AND tray: `agent::host` (prefer ::) over the same federation
  plane. Connected peer (`k2 connections`) is the gate — not a Connect
  host token. Cover .md + small attachments; files stay out of the PTY.
  Wire form fp::ws::agent is `k2 fed send` only, not `k2 msg`.

K2 is source-available Fair Source, not MIT. To change this box, `k2 feedback ask` with a brief (`k2 study ticket-brief`). To talk in this chat, `k2 thread`.

study.title: How to send work
study.summary: k2 msg vs k2 thread vs k2 mail vs talk
study.body:
k2 study send — how to send work

THREE TOOLS (do not mix)
  k2 msg     SEND to another workspace agent: live text OR files
  k2 inbox   YOUR tray (receive / triage). Cannot send a file
  k2 mail    real email (humans / SMTP). Not agents

k2 msg vs k2 thread vs k2 mail
  k2 msg     agent-to-agent. Live line or --inbox-wake / --inbox-silent
  k2 thread  human overlay in this chat (not PTY inject)
  k2 mail    SMTP / hosted / linked inboxes — humans, not agents

LIVE MSG
  Short, one line. `k2 msg <handle> "ready when you are"`
  Sidecar: `k2 msg <handle>/<sidecar> "…"`
  Federated live: `k2 msg <agent>::<host>` (not email).
  Do not paste file contents into live text.

FILES
  `k2 msg <handle> --inbox-wake <path> [path…]`  copy + knock (preferred)
  `k2 msg <handle> --inbox-silent <path> [path…]` copy only; they list
  Bare `--inbox` is an error. Multiple paths → one package, one id.
  Recipient: `k2 inbox list` / `k2 inbox read <id>`.

HUMAN IN THIS CHAT
  A line prefixed `[thread:<addr>]` is the Thread tab. Reply with
  `k2 thread <addr> "…"`. Do not answer in the TUI. Not `k2 msg`.

PROJECT CHAT
  `[project:<name>]` → `k2 project msg <name> "…"`. Never `k2 msg <name>`
  (that looks up a workspace and fails workspace_not_found).

TALK (BETA)
  `k2 talk` is fused read-then-send to another agent (peek the PTY
  first). It is not how you talk to your human.

API CALLER
  If this session is API-launched, only `k2 respond` / `k2 respond --final`
  reaches the caller. They cannot see this terminal. Outside an API
  session `k2 respond` fails loud (needs the staged hook token).

PEEK FIRST
  `k2 read <handle>` peeks their live terminal. Use it before injecting
  when you are not sure they are idle. `k2 talk` fuses read-then-send.

K2 is source-available Fair Source, not MIT. To change this box, `k2 feedback ask` with a brief (`k2 study ticket-brief`). To talk in this chat, `k2 thread`.

study.title: Talking to your human
study.summary: Thread overlay, feedback, [thread:addr]
study.body:
k2 study human — talking to your human

TWO CHANNELS
  k2 thread          this conversation's overlay (Chat / Thread tab)
  k2 feedback ask    a durable item on the Feedback page (survives you)

NOT THESE
  k2 msg     other agents
  k2 talk    fused read+send to another agent's PTY
  k2 mail    real email
  terminal prompts that vanish when the session dies

THREAD
  `k2 thread <addr> "text"`     write overlay (not PTY; that's k2 msg)
  `k2 thread <addr>`            read / tail (default page 25)
  `k2 thread ask <addr> "…" --options a,b,c [--expires 3d]`
                                choice card; returns immediately
  `k2 thread secret <addr> --name NAME`
                                secret field; you never see the value
  `k2 thread void <addr> <card-id>`
                                close your own card (obsolete question)
  `k2 thread <addr> "…" --file docs/report.pdf --file src/a.rs:12-40`
                                attach the files you mention (≤10)

  Same first-arg grammar as msg: sales / sales/reviewer / sales/1.
  Post and continue. Do not --wait. Do not emit widget JSON.
  Your posts may push people's phones: `k2 study notifications`.

CARDS STAY OPEN WHILE PEOPLE TALK
  A person may discuss a card before answering it. Their messages
  never close it and are never its answer. Keep it open and answer
  their questions in prose; they tap when ready. Void your own card
  only when the question is truly obsolete (`k2 thread void`), or post
  a new card if the options changed.

  A card is not an open gate forever: a choice card expires after 7
  days unless you pick a time frame that fits the decision
  (`--expires 2h|3d`, or `--no-expiry`); a secret card after 7 days.
  An expired card says so on the Thread; ask again if you still need it.

ATTACH THE FILES YOU MENTION
  `--file path[:line[-end]]` (repeatable) puts a file chip under your
  message; the person taps it to open the file (on the phone too). It
  is a pointer to this workspace's file, not a copy: it shows "changed"
  after an edit and "not found" when it moves. Only files inside your
  workspace (copy others in first, e.g. out/); secrets are refused
  (.env, keys, tokens, credentials in the text): use `k2 vault`.
  App guests see a file only when their own file access covers it.

[thread:addr]
  If a message arrives prefixed `[thread:<addr>]`, the human wrote on
  the Thread tab. Reply with `k2 thread <addr> "your reply"`.
  Do not answer in this terminal — they are not looking at the TUI.

FEEDBACK
  `k2 feedback ask "<title>" --html brief.html [--body] [--options a,b] [--wait]`
  Files a card your human answers later (or in-session). Use this for
  decisions, approvals, and "please change this box". Attach an HTML
  brief (`k2 tickets template`). See `k2 study feedback-loop` and
  `k2 study ticket-brief`.

WHEN THEY SAY NO VIA THE GATE
  owner_only / gated / forbidden → exit 3. Stop looping. Ask with
  `k2 feedback ask`, do not retry the owner verb.

THREAD VS FEEDBACK
  Thread is this conversation (they may be on the overlay tab).
  Feedback is a card on the Feedback page — use it when the answer
  must survive your session or needs a recorded decision.
  Do not `--wait` on thread ask/secret. Feedback `--wait` is the
  one that blocks on a durable item.

K2 is source-available Fair Source, not MIT. To change this box, `k2 feedback ask` with a brief (`k2 study ticket-brief`). To talk in this chat, `k2 thread`.

study.title: Four people lists
study.summary: Four lists. Never k2 msg usernames
study.body:
k2 study people — four lists (never k2 msg usernames)

There are four different people-shaped lists. Mixing them is the
classic footgun. `k2 msg` talks to connected workspace AGENTS only.

1. CONNECTIONS (AGENTS)
   `k2 connections list`
   Workspace agents this workspace can reach. Handles, not display
   names. This is the yellow pages for `k2 msg` / `k2 read` / `k2 talk`.
   Add/remove may be gated for agents (exit 3). List is always allowed.
   Unconnected live/tray/read → exit 3 `not_connected`.

2. CONNECT USERS
   `k2 connections list --users` (agents) · `k2 users list` (owner/admin)
   Local daemon accounts (owner / admin / member) who log into
   this server. Humans. Not agents. Never `k2 msg` those names.
   `k2 users` is people only (an agent passport exits 3); mutations
   are owner-tier.

3. APP GUESTS
   `k2 app user list` (leftover: `k2 skin user list`)
   App principals — guests for custom UIs that talk to agents
   without a terminal. Capability passes use a k2skn_ prefix and never
   open the grid. Not Connect users. Never `k2 msg` those names.
   See `k2 study apps` (leftover: `k2 study skins`).

4. --users HUMANS
   `k2 connections list --users`
   Humans on this host and their roles (also `k2 agent context add
   users:roster`). Roster for awareness. Never `k2 msg` those names.

RULE
  If it is a username, Connect user, app guest, or `--users` row:
  never `k2 msg` it. Msg handles come from connections (agents).
  Optional context packs: `users:roster`, `apps:roster` (leftover
  `skin:roster`), `connections:roster` — still do not msg humans.

PROJECT NAMES
  A Project is a group of workspaces, not a person and not a
  workspace handle. `[project:<name>]` → `k2 project msg`. Msg'ing
  the project name looks up a workspace and fails.
